title: "capture.output() does not capture messages"

extrait: 'capture.output(message("a"))'

::: {.piege packages="cli"}
```{r}
chatty <- function() {
  print("result")
  message("step done")
  cli::cli_alert_success("All set")
  invisible(NULL)
}
output <- capture.output(chatty())
output
```
:::

## Why

R has two output streams. `print()` and `cat()` write to standard output, which `capture.output()` intercepts. `message()`, `warning()` and {cli} alerts go through the message stream, which always shows on screen and which `capture.output()` ignores by default.

So a function that "prints" something can return an almost empty capture, depending on how its author chose to write it.

## The fix

To collect the messages, intercept them as conditions with `withCallingHandlers()`. `capture.output(type = "message")` also exists, but it diverts the stream itself: it sees nothing as soon as another tool is already intercepting messages, like knitr, which produced this page.

::: {.piege packages="cli"}
```{r}
messages <- character()
output <- withCallingHandlers(
  capture.output(chatty()),
  message = function(m) {
    messages <<- c(messages, conditionMessage(m))
    invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
  }
)
output
messages
```
:::
